answer: Each work enters the anchor registry with a sales royalty pool. A claimant files a vine claim for its key, locks 60, and pays 25. A raven auditor checks the anchor claim against work hash and vine; a duplicate burns the bond. The pool splits equally, so the kth fake still pays 85 while its share falls to pool/k. For a 5,000 pool, 1,000 fakes cost 85,000, gain at most 5,000, and lose 80,000. A royalty-stacking ring fails when raven auditors find identical hashes across many keys, burning all ring bonds. An honest agent files one anchor claim, pays 25, locks 60, and keeps share plus bond.
